label: Chore
description: Small, low-risk maintenance change (deps, docs, config, tooling, CI) with hooks and the full push gate, but without BDD/TDD ceremony; hand off the PR for human review (no auto-merge). If you decide to use sub agents, always set openai-oauth/gpt-5.5 · effort: low.
when_to_use: Use for small maintenance chores with no meaningful behaviour change and low blast radius: dependency bumps, doc fixes, config/CI/tooling tweaks, renames of non-code assets. Do NOT use when the issue's acceptance criteria describe new or altered observable behaviour (use 'feature') or a zero-behaviour-change code restructure (use 'refactor').

guards.message: Complete hook setup, the change itself, and targeted verification before committing.

This workflow does NOT merge — verify the pre-push gate genuinely passed (never bypassed with --no-verify), then report the PR as ready for human review and stop. Never run gh pr merge / git merge or set auto-merge.

steps.label: Scope the chore and define done
steps.guidance: Read the issue and comments with `gh issue view <N> --json title,body,comments` (or restate the ad-hoc request). Write down a short, checkable definition of done and the exact files you expect to touch. If the scope turns out to involve behaviour change, STOP and switch to the 'feature' template instead of stretching this one. Done when the definition of done and file list are written down.

steps.label: Make the minimal change
steps.guidance: Create a branch if on master. Make the smallest change that satisfies the definition of done — no drive-by refactors, no speculative cleanup. Keep repo conventions: if you bump a crate version or touch docs, keep Cargo.toml, README 'Current version' and any version-asserting tests in lockstep. Done when the change matches the definition of done and nothing else changed.

steps.label: Run targeted verification
steps.guidance: Run the narrowest checks that exercise what you touched: targeted `cargo test -p <crate> --lib <name_substring>` for code, the relevant guard tests for docs/config (e.g. repo_docs, workflow_config), or a build/lint for tooling. Do not run the whole suite manually here; label-triggered authoritative CI does that after review. Done when the targeted checks pass and you can name what they proved.

steps.label: Commit and push through the full gate
steps.guidance: Stage only intended files and commit with a clear message. Then `git push` in the FOREGROUND and WAIT for the pre-push gate to exit — it runs the fast local gate and should normally finish within 20 seconds. Fix any failure and push again; never use --no-verify. Done when the push has exited successfully with the gate passing.

steps.label: Open the PR
steps.guidance: Open a PR against master with `gh pr create`: clear title, short body stating what changed and why it is a chore (no behaviour change). Confirm with `gh pr view <n> --json number,headRefOid,state` that the PR is OPEN and its head is your pushed commit. Done when the PR number and head SHA are confirmed.

steps.label: Request authoritative CI and report the PR (no merge)
steps.guidance: After all review comments are resolved and the current head is final, run `gh pr edit <n> --add-label merge-requested`. This requests authoritative CI for that exact revision. Wait with `gh pr checks <n> --watch`; if another commit is pushed, the label is removed automatically and must be reapplied only when ready. Do NOT merge or set auto-merge; report the PR and CI result for human merge.
